selections.justification:
Command Execution: Polarity Bundle polarity mdi polarity auto shutdown polarity mdi polarity auto

[Log-derived analysis] Command-execution resource-usage test for the interface polarity commands (mdi, auto, with an intervening shutdown). With the device in interface-config mode over a bundle of ports, it issues each command, timing execution and measuring the surrounding memory and NSM-message deltas. Reports the measured values and verifies the config is restored to baseline with no exceptions.

step4.objective:
• Half duplex and full duplex each configurable as an explicit fixed value on ports that support them, with the operational duplex matching the configured value.
  • Auto-negotiation reported as disabled on a port carrying an explicit fixed duplex, distinguishing a forced duplex from a negotiated one in the port's reported state.
  • A link established and stable when both ends are fixed to the same duplex, at each speed for which the platform offers that duplex.
  • Half duplex offered only where the port's speed permits it, with the setting rejected or reported as unsupported at speeds where it does not apply.
  • Half-duplex operation exhibiting CSMA/CD behaviour, with collision counters incrementing only under contention and remaining at zero on a full-duplex link.
  • A duplex mismatch between the two ends producing a reported degraded outcome — a link that does not come up, or one whose error counters record the mismatch — rather than silent traffic loss.
  • A duplex value that is invalid, or unsupported on the port's media type, rejected with a clear error, the previous valid configuration remaining in effect.
  • The configured fixed duplex retained across an administrative shutdown/no-shutdown cycle and reapplied from saved configuration after a device restart.
  • The port returned to its default negotiated duplex when the fixed setting is removed or set back to auto.
  • Configured duplex and operational duplex reported consistently in port status and configuration output.

provenance.objective_response:
• Fixed copper 1-Gigabit interfaces accept explicit duplex configuration of half and full at each supported speed (10, 100, 1000 Mbps), with the configured value persisted in the running configuration.
  • Link establishment succeeds between two directly connected fixed copper 1-Gigabit ports configured for forced 10/Half, 100/Half and 1000/Half operation.
  • Link establishment succeeds for the equivalent forced full-duplex combinations (10/Full, 100/Full, 1000/Full), providing the positive baseline against which half-duplex behaviour is compared.
  • Straight-through and crossover copper cabling both yield a working link at each speed/duplex combination, with no dependency on cable pin-out.
  • MDI-to-MDI and MDI-X-to-MDI-X endpoint pairings both reach the linked state at each speed/duplex combination.
  • Manual polarity settings (polarity mdi, polarity mdix) and polarity auto are accepted on the interface and coexist with forced speed and duplex settings without configuration conflict.
  • Automatic polarity resolution selects the correct MDI/MDI-X role for the attached cable type so that the link comes up irrespective of the peer's polarity setting.
  • An interface shutdown followed by no shutdown restores the previously configured speed, duplex and polarity values and re-establishes the link in the same operational state.
  • Negotiated or forced duplex state reported by the interface matches the administratively configured value on both ends of the link.
  • Bidirectional traffic forwarding is achieved at each half-duplex and full-duplex combination, with frames received without loss or corruption at the far end.
  • Half-duplex operation exhibits expected CSMA/CD behaviour, with collision and late-collision counters incrementing only under contended conditions and remaining at zero for full-duplex links.
  • Duplex mismatch between the two endpoints results in the expected degraded outcome — link up with error counters incrementing or link not established — rather than silent traffic loss without indication.
  • Speed or duplex values not supported on the fixed copper 1-Gigabit interface are rejected with a clear error message, and the prior valid configuration remains in effect.
  • 1000 Mbps half-duplex is handled consistently with the platform's documented support position — either operational as configured or rejected with an explicit unsupported indication.
  • Transitions between speed/duplex/polarity combinations occur without interface lock-up, requiring no device reload to recover a usable link.
  • Interface status output reports speed, duplex, polarity/MDI role, administrative state and operational state consistently across all tested combinations.
  • Link state changes and duplex-related errors generate corresponding log entries and counter updates that accurately reflect the observed physical-layer events.
  • Configuration survives a device restart, with the saved speed, duplex and polarity settings reapplied and the link re-established without manual intervention.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.

On a copper port that supports both duplex modes, configure an explicit fixed half duplex and then an explicit fixed full duplex, at each speed the platform offers for that media. Confirm the operational duplex matches the configured value in each case and that the port's reported state shows auto-negotiation as disabled while a fixed duplex is in effect.

With the DUT and a link partner connected over a copper link, fix both ends to the same duplex at each supported speed — including half duplex at the lower speeds and full duplex across the range —. Confirm the link comes up and remains stable, and that both ends report the same operational speed and duplex.

Attempt to configure half duplex on a port running at a speed where the platform does not offer half duplex. Confirm the DUT either rejects the setting or reports it as unsupported, and that the port's prior speed/duplex configuration remains in effect.

Establish a half-duplex link between the DUT and a partner and drive bidirectional traffic from both ends simultaneously to create contention on the shared medium. Confirm collision-related counters on the half-duplex port increment under contention, then repeat the same traffic profile over a full-duplex link and confirm those counters stay at zero.

Create a duplex mismatch by fixing one end to full duplex and the other end to half duplex on the same link, at a speed where both modes are supported. Confirm the outcome is reported — either the link does not come up, or the port's error counters record the mismatch while traffic is offered — rather than passing silently.

Attempt to configure a duplex value that is invalid, and a duplex value that is valid in general but unsupported on the port's media type (for example a fibre or SFP-based port that offers only one duplex mode). Confirm each attempt is rejected with a clear error and the port's previously configured duplex remains in effect and operational.

With a fixed duplex configured on a linked port, administratively shut down the port and bring it back up. Confirm the configured duplex is retained across the cycle and that the link re-establishes at the same duplex without reverting to negotiation.

Save the running configuration with fixed duplex settings applied on multiple ports, including at least one half-duplex port, then restart the device. Confirm each port's duplex configuration is reapplied from saved configuration after boot and that the operational duplex matches on link-up.

Remove the fixed duplex setting from a port, or set it back to auto, while the link partner remains connected. Confirm the port returns to its default negotiated duplex, that auto-negotiation is once again reported as enabled, and that the link re-establishes at the negotiated speed and duplex.

For a port under each configuration state exercised above — fixed half, fixed full, and auto — cross-check the port status reporting against the configuration output. Confirm the configured duplex and the operational duplex are reported consistently between the two, including on a port that is administratively down or has no link partner.

gaps: The selected ART coverage (1342.301.13) exercises polarity-related command execution — MDI and auto polarity settings applied and re-applied across a shutdown boundary — so it reasonably addresses CLI acceptance, configuration persistence, and basic polarity state handling on a fixed copper interface. It does not, however, drive the half-duplex dimension that defines this case: the manual TestLink and Zephyr artefacts pair explicit speed and duplex forcing (10/Half, 100/Half, 1000/Half) with fixed MDI-to-MDI and MDIX-to-MDIX polarity combinations on both DUT and partner, which the automation neither configures nor observes. Consequently the negative-link expectation seen in the straight-cable 10/Half MDI-to-MDI scenario, and the corresponding link-up-with-matching-speed/duplex/polarity outcomes on the crossover variants, remain unautomated, as does any confirmation that the negotiated operational state on the link partner agrees with the forced local configuration. Cabling topology (straight versus crossover) and the presence of a correctly configured partner device are likewise outside the automated harness, leaving duplex-mismatch and polarity-mismatch interactions to manual execution.
